Core rules for paperwork queues in detail
This section sets out why careful work counts

Companion Animal Travel Desk paper queue control

This section sets out the rules for handling travel files so that every pet journey is tracked cleanly from booking through pickup. The desk must keep paperwork current, legible, and ready for the next handoff, because delays in review can interrupt care and create avoidable risk for the traveler and the owner.

All incoming forms must be checked at once for complete contact details, carrier notes, feeding instructions, and any required travel approvals. If a form is unclear, the agent must pause the file, add a clear note, and move it to the correction stack without delay. The service depends on careful sorting, so urgent items stay visible and ordinary files do not get buried under new arrivals.

When a pet record is updated, the change must be reflected in every working copy used by the desk. Staff should keep language brief, kind, and factual. No guesswork is allowed where a carrier, health note, or pickup instruction is missing. If a traveler arrives with new paperwork, the agent must place it with the active file and inform the senior coordinator so the record stays aligned.

Files ready for review must be passed forward in good order, with all pages attached and any exception clearly marked. If a record is held back, the reason must be written plainly so the next worker can act without confusion. Shared responsibility is the standard here, and every handoff must support that standard without exception.

If the desk cannot resolve a paperwork issue at once, contact the senior coordinator or the duty supervisor at once.
